name: application-booking-search-bar
title: Booking Search Bar
description: A combined location, date-range, and guest-count search widget for travel or reservation booking flows, in a pill-segmented horizontal bar and a stacked card layout.
useWhen: A travel, hospitality, or reservation site needs a single combined search entry point for where/when/how-many, rather than separate unconnected fields.
Search inputs benefit from being visually unified as one control (single border, single shadow) instead of a generic form row.
avoidWhen: You need to filter already-loaded results by applied criteria — use data-filter-bar for that layer instead.
Only one or two search dimensions are needed — a simpler combobox or date-range picker alone may be sufficient.
responsiveBehavior: The horizontal variant is a single pill-shaped row divided into four label/input segments plus a trailing search button, intended for wide viewports; the stacked variant collapses the same four fields into a bordered card with a full-width search button below, suited to narrow viewports.
accessibility: Each segment is a real <label> wrapping its input, so the small eyebrow text (Where, Check in, Check out, Who) is the input's accessible name, not just decorative text.
The search trigger is a real <button type="submit">; the icon-only horizontal variant carries an aria-label since it has no visible text.
Segments are visually separated with dividers so keyboard and screen reader users can perceive the same four-part structure sighted users see.
